issues.legal_issue: A conviction under an unconstitutional mandatory-capital-punishment provision cannot stand and must be replaced by a conviction under the general murder provision.
material_facts: The appellant was convicted under Section 303 of the Indian Penal Code for murder while serving a life sentence for an earlier murder.
Section 303 had been declared void as violating Articles 14 and 21 of the Constitution.
issues.conclusion: The conviction under Section 303 could not stand and was altered to a conviction under Section 302 of the Indian Penal Code.
issues.legal_principle: Because Section 303 of the Indian Penal Code was held void for violating Articles 14 and 21 of the Constitution, the conviction under it could not stand; the murder conviction was instead entered under Section 302. No earlier cases are cited in the supplied judgment.

predicates.criminal_appeal_from_conviction: The matter is an appeal challenging a criminal conviction.
predicates.conviction_under_mandatory_capital_murde: The appellant was convicted under a provision that required capital punishment for the offense.
predicates.capital_murder_provision_declared_uncons: The provision under which the appellant was convicted had been declared unconstitutional.

issues.definition: When a criminal appeal challenges a conviction under an unconstitutional provision requiring capital punishment, the conviction is replaced by one under the general murder offense.

issues.legal_issue: The appropriate punishment for murder must be assessed in light of the circumstances of the offense, and death was not warranted in this case.
material_facts: The appellant committed the murder within about a month after release on parole, a circumstance the State relied on in seeking the death penalty.
The assault was immediately connected to a dispute over a power of attorney executed by the appellant’s father and challenged by the father’s two brothers.
The appellant assaulted the deceased with the blunt side of a gandasa.
issues.conclusion: The extreme penalty of death was not warranted; the appellant was sentenced to imprisonment for life under Section 302 of the Indian Penal Code.
issues.legal_principle: In imposing punishment for murder under Section 302 of the Indian Penal Code, the court considered the circumstances that immediately led to the assault and the use of the blunt side of the weapon. No earlier cases are cited in the supplied judgment.

rule.if: criminal_appeal_from_murder_sentence and murder_conviction and immediate_property_dispute_precipitated_assault and blunt_side_of_weapon_used

predicates.criminal_appeal_from_murder_sentence: The matter is an appeal challenging the sentence for murder.
predicates.murder_conviction: The appellant stands convicted of murder.
predicates.immediate_property_dispute_precipitated_: A dispute concerning property or a related instrument was the immediate cause of the assault.
predicates.blunt_side_of_weapon_used: The assailant used the blunt side of a weapon in the assault.

issues.definition: When a murder-sentence appeal concerns an offense immediately precipitated by a property dispute and involving use of a weapon’s blunt side, the sentence is life imprisonment rather than death.

issues.legal_issue: A shared intention to kill supports joint murder liability even when the other participants inflicted only simple injuries with the blunt side of a weapon.
material_facts: The other appellants accompanied the principal appellant at midnight and were found to share the intention to kill the deceased.
The other appellants had assaulted the deceased with the blunt side of the gandasa and were said to have inflicted only simple injuries.
Their argument that they should instead be convicted only for causing simple hurt was rejected.
issues.conclusion: The convictions and life sentences of the other appellants under Sections 302 and 34 of the Indian Penal Code were confirmed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 302 and 34 of the Indian Penal Code, participants who share the intention to cause death may be held jointly liable for murder; the court rejected reduction to Section 323 where that common intention was established. No earlier cases are cited in the supplied judgment.

predicates.criminal_appeal_from_joint_murder_convic: The matter is an appeal challenging a joint murder conviction.
predicates.common_intention_to_kill_established: The participants shared an intention to kill the victim.
predicates.participants_jointly_accompanied_princip: The participants accompanied the principal offender while taking part in the incident.
predicates.blunt_side_of_weapon_used: The participants used the blunt side of a weapon in the assault.
predicates.only_simple_injuries_inflicted: The participants’ own blows inflicted only simple injuries.

issues.definition: When participants in an appeal against a joint murder conviction accompanied the principal offender and shared an intention to kill, their joint murder conviction and sentence remain confirmed even if their blows used a weapon’s blunt side or inflicted only simple injuries.

issues.legal_issue: A new life sentence imposed on a person already serving imprisonment may be directed to run from the date of the trial court’s conviction, with the applicable release restriction remaining in force.
material_facts: The appellant was already serving a sentence of imprisonment when the new life sentence was imposed.
The court considered the length of time the appellant had already spent in jail.
The court directed the new life sentence to run from the date of conviction by the Sessions Court and stated that Section 433A of the Code of Criminal Procedure would apply.
issues.conclusion: The appellant’s life sentence for the present offense was directed to run from the date of conviction by the Sessions Court, and Section 433A of the Code of Criminal Procedure was to apply.
issues.legal_principle: The court relied on the appellant’s existing imprisonment and the time already spent in jail to direct when the new life sentence would run; it also applied Section 433A of the Code of Criminal Procedure. No earlier cases are cited in the supplied judgment.

issues.definition: When a criminal appeal imposes a new life sentence on an appellant already serving imprisonment after substantial time in jail, the sentence runs from the trial court’s conviction and the applicable release restrictions remain in force.
